elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Paragraph 14 requires "comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)" but states no per-occurrence basis; the limit could be read as a single aggregate limit. The per-occurrence anchor is absent from the operative text.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No aggregate limit appears anywhere in Paragraph 14 as rendered; only a single USD 1,000,000 CGL figure is stated.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered text keeps E&O at "at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)", below the preferred USD 2,000,000 floor.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cover is "cyber and privacy liability insurance with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000)", short of the preferred USD 5,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: "At Company's request, Contractor shall provide Company with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance or self-insurance evidencing the above coverage".

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Retained language: "professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)" — meets the USD 1M floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted into the same maintenance obligation: "and cyber and privacy liability insurance with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000)", carried by Contractor throughout the term and covered by the certificates-on-request sentence.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the retained E&O limit of USD 1,000,000 satisfies the first fallback element and the inserted cyber and privacy liability limit of USD 2,000,000 satisfies the second; both sit inside the existing 'Contractor shall maintain ... throughout the term' obligation and are captured by the existing certificate-on-request sentence, so no undefined trigger or dangling reference arises.

Preferred is not complete: CGL lacks a per-occurrence basis and any aggregate limit, E&O remains at USD 1,000,000 rather than USD 2,000,000, and cyber is USD 2,000,000 rather than USD 5,000,000. To reach preferred the drafter would need to render 'commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate', raise E&O to USD 2,000,000 and cyber to USD 5,000,000.

Minimal: the edit is a single conjunctive insertion of the one missing fallback coverage into the existing list. No survival tail, at-own-expense language, notice mechanic or other model-language extra was imported, and no existing Customer-favourable wording (workers' comp, certificates, prompt notice of material change) was deleted or paraphrased.

Preserves intent: the cyber limit is not conditioned on selected named data categories, the 'in connection with the provision of Services' qualifier and all other Paragraph 14 mechanics survive without contradiction, and Paragraph 1(c) facility/system-access obligations are untouched.

Classification as a deviation is correct: before the edit the clause failed the fallback on a material term (no cyber or privacy cover for a contractor whose personnel access Company facilities and computer systems), which is not a mere sub-element shortfall.
